correctness.rationale: Orient each edge away from its star center; conversely, split each vertex's outgoing edges into stars of sizes k and k+1. This is equivalent to all outdegrees lying in the nonnegative semigroup they generate. The quotient–remainder representation proves the conductor k(k−1), with predecessor excluded by its residue. If a shore size is represented, a one-way orientation suffices; otherwise both sizes come from the finite positive gap lists below the conductor. Recomputed coverage consists of three exceptional pairs for k=4 and nine for k=5. An independent replay using dynamic-programming semigroup generation checked every row and column outdegree of the twelve frozen orientations and all twelve passed. Replay: /workspace/branches/6e55ef8d-6f98-43f7-9735-5e37d4fbd7c3/replay_record2.py and replay_record2.out in the same directory. The original verifier was inspected, not executed. This finite replay is sufficient only in combination with the analytic reduction. In K_{k−1,k(k−1)−1}, the larger shore's vertices have degree <k and must all be leaves, leaving forbidden outdegree k(k−1)−1 on the smaller shore; this proves the all-k lower bound analytically. The threshold concerns only positive shore sizes and does not require both star sizes to occur.
